# Figures: everything is an SVG

**One rule above all the others: a figure is an SVG, generated by a script,
and editable by hand afterwards.** Those three things are not in tension and
the setup here keeps all of them true at once.

    cd paper && make figures       # rebuild every figure in the paper

Output lands in `paper/figures/svg/`. That is the deliverable — open any of
them in Inkscape, change what you like, save. PDFs beside them in
`paper/figures/pdf/` are derived and disposable.

## Why SVG rather than a PDF out of LaTeX

A figure assembled in the document can only be edited by editing the document.
An SVG can be opened, nudged, relabelled and handed to a collaborator by
someone who does not build the paper at all. The script stays the source of
truth for the data; the SVG is where human judgement gets applied on top.

## The three things that make an SVG actually editable

Generating an SVG is not enough. All three of these had to be set, and a
figure fails the "can I edit this" test if any one regresses.

**1. Text must be text.** matplotlib defaults to `svg.fonttype: "path"`, which
converts every label to outlines. The figure looks identical and is completely
uneditable — fixing a typo means redrawing the glyph. `palette.py` sets
`"none"`, so labels are real `<text>` elements.

    grep -c '<text' paper/figures/svg/fig3_momi.svg    # must be > 0

**2. The font must resolve to what laid it out.** With `fonttype: none` the
SVG carries a font *name* and the editor resolves it; if matplotlib laid out
with a different font than Inkscape renders, every label shifts. Verified:
Arial is installed at `/usr/share/fonts/windows/arial.ttf` and is what
matplotlib resolves, and the fallbacks (Liberation, Nimbus, DejaVu) are
metrically compatible. **If you change the font stack, re-check this.**

**3. Dense marks must be rasterised.** Figure 3's strip plots are ~3,300
points per panel; as vectors that is ~6,600 separate objects, slow to open and
miserable to select around. `rasterized=True` collapses each cloud to one
image object while axes, ticks and text stay vector.

    grep -c '<use ' paper/figures/svg/fig3_momi.svg    # keep in the low hundreds

Rule of thumb: anything above a few hundred marks gets `rasterized=True`.

## House typography

Set in `paper/figures/palette.py`, applied on import. Import it before
plotting and it is handled.

| | |
|---|---|
| page width | `PAGE_WIDTH_IN = 6.5` (letter, 1 in margins) |
| font floor | `MIN_FONT = 7.0`, via `fs()` |
| panel letters | `PANEL_LABEL_PT = 9.0`, bold |
| font | Arial, black, with metrically-compatible fallbacks |
| corners | square everywhere (`legend.fancybox: False`) |

**Use `fs(size)` for every font size rather than writing the number.** A floor
that lives in a comment gets broken the first time a label needs to squeeze
into a corner.

**A font floor only means anything at print width.** A figure authored 13.5 in
wide and placed at `\textwidth` is scaled by 0.48, so its 8 pt labels arrive at
3.9 pt. `figio.save` warns with the arithmetic when a figure is authored wider
than the page. Author at 6.5 in.

## Always save through `figio.save`

    from figio import save
    save(fig, "my_figure")        # -> figures/svg/my_figure.svg (+ pdf)

It rejects any extension but `.svg`, warns about the width problem above, and
writes the PDF alongside so the build does not depend on Inkscape being
installed (it is not, on every machine this paper builds on).

Never call `fig.savefig` directly — a script that writes a PNG puts a file
into the build that nothing knows how to regenerate.

## Colour

From `palette.py`, not invented per figure. `FRAGMENT` is the first four of
`ORDERED`; `PALETTE["purple"]` is the reserved fifth slot (the MoMI library
has five); `SEQUENTIAL` is a six-step blue ramp for ordered quantities such as
rounds. Greys are for rules and de-emphasis, never for a data series that
needs identity.

## Layout traps that cost real time here

- **`bbox_inches="tight"` makes figure width content-dependent**, so one stray
  element silently sets the whole figure's edge. Use fixed margins and
  `tight=False` when width must be constant across figures.
- **Aspect-equal axes are fitted and centred**, so excess row height becomes
  dead band split above and below. That is a `height_ratios` problem, not a
  spacing one — changing `hspace` will do nothing.
- **`ax.get_tightbbox` under-measures rotated text** (386.8 px reported against
  400.2 px actual for a y-label), which is why panel letters land on y-labels.
  Union the tight bbox with the explicit text extents.
- **Panel letters can land off-canvas** with `tight=False` and nothing will
  say so. Look at the rendered file.

## After you change a figure

1. `cd paper && make figures` — all six must print OK.
2. Open the SVG, or render it, **and look at it**. No audit catches label
   collisions and overflow.
3. If the paper still builds from it: `pdflatex clean.tex`, expect 0 errors
   and 0 overfull boxes.

## Data gating (Figure 3)

`momi_fragments.py` and `fig3_momi.py` are both gated to
`second_big_library`. The two PETase libraries share 5 parts out of 3,629, so
pooling is wrong rather than noisy — drawn over both, slots 2 and 3 read 8.1
and 7.0 mean mutations against the true 4.4 and 4.4. Every table Figure 3
reads goes through one `only()` helper that exits if the filter leaves
nothing, so a new panel cannot quietly skip it.

## Archive

Superseded scripts are in `paper/figures/archive/`, with a README saying which
are parked broken rather than parked working. The live set is the transitive
closure of local imports from the figures the paper builds — note `ame_fragk`
looks dead and is not.
